discovery: Emergent magnetic monopoles and the Coulomb phase in spin ice

nominees.name: Roderich Moessner
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden

motivation: Castelnovo, Moessner and Sondhi showed (Nature 2008) that the elementary excitations of spin ice pyrochlores such as Dy2Ti2O7 and Ho2Ti2O7 are deconfined magnetic monopoles: fractionalised quasiparticles carrying magnetic charge and interacting through a magnetic Coulomb law. Building on the emergent gauge-field (Coulomb phase) description of the ice rules, their work made a concrete, quantitative prediction for real crystals. It was confirmed directly by polarized and diffuse neutron scattering, which revealed pinch-point singularities and Dirac-string correlations, and by magnetisation, muon and noise measurements. The discovery established that emergent gauge fields and fractionalised excitations, long theoretical ideas, appear in ordinary magnetic materials. It created the field of 'magnetricity', shaped the search for quantum spin ices and spin liquids, and remains a model of how theory and microscopic measurement on real crystals together reveal new states of matter.
